summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of hypogammaglobulinemia, mitochondrial disease, and coronary artery disease was admitted for observation during a scheduled IVIG infusion. He had a low-grade fever on admission, which resolved with Tylenol; chest X-ray and cultures showed no infection. He received 2 liters of saline before the infusion and was pre-medicated with Benadryl and Tylenol. During the IVIG infusion, he developed mild shortness of breath, improved with 2 liters of oxygen, but remained stable without hypoxia or cardiac symptoms. He tolerated the half-dose regimen well, with fewer side effects than in prior infusions. No medication changes were made. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue outpatient IVIG, fluid boluses, and follow-up with specialists.
